fields.Notes: Lady Churchill had his 1954 portrait of her husband destroyed; the Coventry tapestry is 23 metres high and was woven at Felletin in France.
fields.Description: English painter of thorn trees, gnarled roots and bomb-wrecked streets as menacing, half-organic forms, who designed the vast Christ in Glory tapestry for Coventry Cathedral and a Churchill portrait the family burned.
fields.Captions: Graham Sutherland, Devastation, 1941: East End, Wrecked Public House | Christ in Glory in the Tetramorph, Coventry Cathedral
fields.Works: Christ in Glory in the Tetramorph, the Coventry tapestry; Thorn Trees; the Devastation series; Somerset Maugham

fields.Title: Yves Tanguy
fields.Notes: He decided to become a painter after glimpsing a de Chirico in a dealer's window from a moving bus; he married the American Surrealist Kay Sage.
fields.Description: Self-taught French Surrealist who painted the same picture all his life: a vast, empty, evenly lit plain under a graded sky, scattered with smooth bone- or pebble-like objects casting long shadows.
fields.Captions: Yves Tanguy, Indefinite Divisibility, 1942
fields.Works: Indefinite Divisibility; Mama, Papa is Wounded!; The Furniture of Time; Multiplication of the Arcs

fields.Title: Antoni Tàpies
fields.Notes: He co-founded the Catalan avant-garde group Dau al Set in 1948; a foundation in his own Barcelona building has held his work since 1990.
fields.Description: Catalan painter of thick, wall-like surfaces mixed with marble dust, sand, and straw, then scratched and scored with crosses, footprints, and graffiti -- decay and endurance under Franco's Spain.
fields.Captions: Antoni Tàpies
fields.Works: Grey and Green Painting; Great Painting; Matter in the Form of a Foot; Rinzen

fields.Title: Maurice Utrillo
fields.Notes: Son of Suzanne Valadon, born when she was 18; he took the surname of a Spanish critic who agreed to acknowledge him, and the “white period” of 1909-14 is the prized one.
fields.Description: French painter of the streets of one Paris hill -- empty roads, plaster walls, the Sacré-Cœur, a lopsided sign -- worked in chalky whites during his best period, which he took up as a cure for alcoholism.
fields.Captions: Maurice Utrillo, c. 1915–20
fields.Works: La Maison Rose; Rue Saint-Rustique; Sacré-Cœur de Montmartre; the Montmagny views

fields.Title: Suzanne Valadon
fields.Notes: The first woman admitted to the Société Nationale des Beaux-Arts, in 1894; Degas bought her drawings and encouraged her, and Maurice Utrillo was her son.
fields.Description: French painter who began as a circus acrobat and then an artists' model -- for Renoir, Puvis de Chavannes, and Toulouse-Lautrec -- and taught herself to paint blunt, hard-outlined female nudes with no flattery at all.
fields.Captions: Self-portrait
fields.Works: The Blue Room; Adam and Eve; The Abandoned Doll; Nude Sitting on a Sofa

fields.Title: Keith Vaughan
fields.Notes: Largely self-taught, he served in the Pioneer Corps as a conscientious objector; the journals, published after his death, are now the most-read part of his work.
fields.Description: English painter of male nudes and bathers dissolved into landscape in increasingly abstract slabs of grey-green colour, who kept a journal about being gay before decriminalization and recorded his own suicide in its last entry.
fields.Captions: Keith Vaughan, A Barrack-room (Imperial War Museum)
fields.Works: Assembly of Figures series; Landscape with Bathers; the Festival of Britain mural; Theseus

fields.Title: Alfred Wallis
fields.Notes: He said he painted “what used to be” -- the sailing ships of his youth -- and died in the Madron workhouse; Bernard Leach made the tiles for his grave.
fields.Description: Cornish mariner and marine-stores dealer who started painting at 70 with ship's paint on scraps of cardboard, ignoring scale and perspective entirely; found in St Ives by Ben Nicholson and Christopher Wood.
fields.Captions: Alfred Wallis, Hold House Port Mear Square Island
fields.Works: St Ives; Hold House Port Mear Square Island; Two Ships and Steamer; The Blue Ship

fields.Title: Alison Wilding
fields.Notes: One of the New British Sculpture generation with Cragg, Deacon, and Woodrow; shortlisted for the Turner Prize in 1988 and 1992, and elected a Royal Academician in 1999.
fields.Description: English sculptor who sets opposed materials against each other -- alabaster against rubber, beaten lead against brass, wax against steel -- in quiet, tightly made abstract pieces of no great size.
fields.Captions: Alison Wilding, On the Day, Tate Liverpool
fields.Works: Assembly; Hand to Mouth; On the Day; Swarm

fields.Title: David Wilkie
fields.Notes: Wellington commissioned the Waterloo picture, and a rail had to be put up to hold back the crowds at the 1822 Academy; he died at sea off Gibraltar, and Turner painted the burial.
fields.Description: Scottish painter whose crowded, anecdotal village scenes -- a rent day, a blind fiddler, pensioners reading the Waterloo dispatch -- made genre painting respectable in Britain and were engraved by the thousand.
fields.Captions: Self-portrait
fields.Works: The Chelsea Pensioners Reading the Waterloo Dispatch; The Blind Fiddler; Village Politicians; Distraining for Rent

fields.Title: Richard Wilson
fields.Notes: Turner and Constable both took him as the founder of British landscape painting; he died poor and largely forgotten in Denbighshire.
fields.Description: Welsh painter, a founder member of the Royal Academy, who applied the golden light and classical composition of Claude to the Thames valley, Snowdonia, and Rome, and made landscape a serious British subject.
fields.Captions: Richard Wilson, painted by Anton Raphael Mengs
fields.Works: Snowdon from Llyn Nantlle; The Destruction of the Children of Niobe; Rome from the Villa Madama; Holt Bridge on the River Dee

fields.Title: Konrad Witz
fields.Notes: The Miraculous Draught of 1444 sets Christ on the shore of Lake Geneva with the Mole and the Petit Salève clearly recognisable behind him.
fields.Description: German-Swiss painter working in Basel who gave his figures heavy, sculptural, awkwardly solid bodies, and painted what is usually called the first accurate topographical landscape in European art -- a real, identifiable stretch of Lake Geneva.
fields.Captions: Konrad Witz, Saint Christopher, Kunstmuseum Basel | The Miraculous Draught of Fishes, 1444
fields.Works: The Miraculous Draught of Fishes, from the Altarpiece of St Peter; Saint Christopher; The Synagogue; the Heilsspiegel Altarpiece

fields.Title: Bill Woodrow
fields.Notes: One of the New British Sculpture generation; Regardless of History occupied the Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square in 2000.
fields.Description: English sculptor who cut new shapes out of scrapped consumer goods -- a washing machine, a car bonnet, a twin-tub, an ironing board -- leaving the cut-out still umbilically attached to the object it came from.
fields.Captions: Bill Woodrow
fields.Works: Twin-Tub with Guitar; Elephant; Car Door, Ironing Board and Twin-Tub with North American Indian Head-dress; Regardless of History

fields.Title: Jack B. Yeats
fields.Notes: The Liffey Swim won a silver medal in the art competitions at the 1924 Paris Olympics; Beckett and Kokoschka both wrote in his praise.
fields.Description: Irish painter, brother of a far more famous poet, who moved from black-and-white illustration of fairs, races, and tinkers to late canvases of thick, wild, palette-knifed colour in which the figures nearly dissolve.
fields.Captions: Jack B. Yeats
fields.Works: The Liffey Swim; Men of Destiny; Grief; A Race in Hy-Brazil

fields.Title: Johan Zoffany
fields.Notes: Queen Charlotte disliked the Tribuna for the number of English gentlemen he had crowded into it; he spent six years in India painting for the Company's officers.
fields.Description: German-born painter in England, India, and Italy of theatrical scenes and elaborate group portraits -- connoisseurs crowded round the Venus de' Medici, the Royal Academicians at a life class, a nabob's household at Lucknow.
fields.Captions: Self-Portrait as David with the Head of Goliath | The Tribuna of the Uffizi, 1772–77
fields.Works: The Tribuna of the Uffizi; The Academicians of the Royal Academy; David Garrick in 'The Farmer's Return'; Colonel Mordaunt's Cock Match

fields.Title: Cave paintings at Altamira
fields.Captions: Polychrome bison on the cave ceiling, in ochre and charcoal, using the rock's own bulges for the animals' backs.

fields.Title: Prince Rahotep and his wife Nofret
fields.Captions: Painted limestone pair statue from their tomb at Meidum; the inlaid rock-crystal eyes reportedly terrified the workmen who found them.

fields.Title: Chinese bronze ritual vessels
fields.Captions: Shang and Zhou vessels for offerings of food and wine, cast in piece moulds and covered in taotie monster masks.

fields.Title: Chinese jade ornament
fields.Captions: A Neolithic Liangzhu bi: a pierced disc of nephrite, worked without metal tools and buried with the dead.

fields.Title: Assyrian lion hunt reliefs
fields.Captions: Gypsum panels from Ashurbanipal's palace at Nineveh: the king kills lions released from cages, as a display of royal power.

fields.Title: Laocoön and His Sons
fields.Artist: Hagesandros, Athanadoros and Polydoros of Rhodes
fields.Captions: The Trojan priest and his sons crushed by sea serpents; dug up in Rome in 1506 and famous within days.

fields.Title: Standing Buddha from Gandhara
fields.Captions: A Buddha in Greek-style drapery from the north-west of the subcontinent, where Hellenistic and Indian traditions met.

fields.Title: Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius
fields.Captions: The only bronze equestrian statue to survive from antiquity, spared because the Middle Ages took it for Constantine.

fields.Title: Teotihuacan mask
fields.Captions: A stone funerary mask with hollow eyes once inlaid with shell and obsidian; it has no eyeholes and was never worn.

fields.Title: Sarcophagus of Junius Bassus
fields.Location: Museo Storico del Tesoro della Basilica di San Pietro, Rome
fields.Captions: A Roman prefect's marble coffin, its two tiers of columned niches holding scenes from both Testaments.

fields.Title: Mosaics of Emperor Justinian and Empress Theodora
fields.Captions: Facing panels in San Vitale, Ravenna: emperor and empress bring offerings, frontal and weightless on a gold ground.

fields.Title: Gero Cross
fields.Captions: A near-life-size oak crucifix in Cologne Cathedral, the earliest large sculpture of the dead Christ in the West.

fields.Title: Mihrab of the Great Mosque of Córdoba
fields.Captions: The prayer niche in its horseshoe-arched bay, faced with gold mosaic sent by the Byzantine emperor.

fields.Title: Shiva Nataraja
fields.Captions: Shiva dancing the destruction and renewal of the universe inside a ring of flame; a Chola bronze cast by lost wax.

fields.Title: Nio temple guardians
fields.Captions: The two wrathful guardians of the Great South Gate at Tōdai-ji, carved from joined blocks in about seventy days.

fields.Title: Stained-glass windows of Chartres Cathedral
fields.Captions: Notre-Dame de la Belle Verrière; the deep blue is the colour Chartres is known for and has never been exactly reproduced.

fields.Title: Pisa Baptistery pulpit
fields.Captions: A hexagonal marble pulpit on columns, its reliefs copied from Roman sarcophagi -- Italian sculpture beginning to recover antiquity.

fields.Title: Renunciation of Worldly Goods
fields.Captions: Bardi Chapel fresco: Francis strips naked in front of his father, and the bishop covers him with a cloak.

fields.Title: Wind among the Trees on the Riverbank
fields.Location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York City
fields.Captions: Dry brush, very little ink, and an empty middle distance; the Yuan literati painted for each other rather than for a patron.

fields.Title: The Wilton Diptych
fields.Captions: A portable altarpiece for Richard II, who kneels before eleven angels all wearing his own white hart badge.

fields.Title: Cecilia Gonzaga medal
fields.Captions: A cast bronze portrait medal; the reverse shows a unicorn and a moon, emblems of the sitter's chastity.

fields.Title: Coatlicue
fields.Location: National Museum of Anthropology, Mexico City
fields.Captions: The Aztec earth goddess, whose name is Nahuatl for “serpent skirt.” Decapitated, she has twin snake heads, a necklace of hands and hearts, and clawed feet.

fields.Title: Young Man Among Roses
fields.Captions: A portrait miniature about two and a half inches high, the sitter leaning among eglantine, in watercolour and gold on vellum.

fields.Title: Akbar's Adventures with the Elephant Hawa'i
fields.Captions: A double page from the Akbarnama: the young emperor rides a maddened elephant across a bridge of boats.

fields.Title: Christ of Clemency
fields.Captions: A polychrome wooden crucifix for Seville Cathedral, contracted to show Christ still alive and looking down at the worshipper.

fields.Title: Landscape with Ascanius Shooting the Stag of Silvia
fields.Captions: Claude's last painting: the shot from the Aeneid that starts a war, buried inside a still golden landscape.

fields.Title: Adoration of the Name of Jesus
fields.Captions: The nave ceiling of the Gesù in Rome, painted so that the figures spill over the frame in stucco and out into the church.

fields.Title: Palazzo Farnese ceiling
fields.Captions: The Loves of the Gods, framed as though they were separate easel paintings hung on the vault.

fields.Title: The Avenue at Middelharnis
fields.Captions: A dead-straight avenue of thin alders running to the horizon, with the vanishing point on the skyline.

fields.Title: Diana after the Bath
fields.Captions: Rococo mythology as a pretext: the goddess and a nymph on silk beside the spoils of the hunt.

fields.Title: A Vase of Flowers
fields.Captions: The painter's only known flower piece, built from soft dry touches, in a blue-and-white Delft vase.

fields.Title: Goethe in the Roman Campagna
fields.Captions: The poet reclining in a white cloak among broken antiquity, painted during his Italian journey.

fields.Title: Character Heads
fields.Captions: One of 69 busts of grimacing faces in lead and alabaster, made in isolation and never commissioned by anyone.

fields.Title: Tintern Abbey
fields.Captions: An early watercolour of the roofless abbey, with ivy and saplings growing up through the nave.

fields.Title: Hambletonian, Rubbing Down
fields.Captions: The racehorse after a punishing match, held by a groom and a stable lad; the painter had to sue his patron to be paid.

fields.Title: The Disasters of War
fields.Captions: One of 82 etchings of atrocity in the Peninsular War, left unpublished for 35 years after the artist's death.

fields.Title: Lion Crushing a Serpent
fields.Captions: A bronze animal fight, the lion sometimes read as the July Monarchy crushing its enemies.

fields.Title: Boulevard du Temple
fields.Captions: A daguerreotype of a busy street that looks deserted: only a man having his boots polished stood still long enough to register.

fields.Title: Napoleon Awakening to Immortality
fields.Captions: The emperor rising from his shroud on a rock, carved for a veteran's private park at Fixin.

fields.Title: The Romans of the Decadence
fields.Captions: An orgy staged among statues of the republican virtues; a Salon sensation read as a verdict on Louis-Philippe's France.

fields.Title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake
fields.Captions: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo; the rain is cut as fine lines straight across the block. Van Gogh copied it in oils.

fields.Title: Surprised!
fields.Captions: A tiger in a storm, built from layers of green by a self-taught toll collector who never left France.

fields.Title: Day of the God
fields.Captions: Tahitians beside a pool of enamel-flat colour, with an invented idol of the moon goddess Hina behind them.

fields.Title: Gismonda
fields.Captions: The poster made overnight for Sarah Bernhardt: life-size, narrow, pale, and the start of Art Nouveau graphics.

fields.Title: Tomb of Oscar Wilde
fields.Captions: A winged demon-angel in Hopton Wood stone at Père Lachaise; its genitals were removed after complaints.

fields.Title: Composition VI
fields.Captions: The painter worked at it for six months, got nowhere, and finished in three days after saying the word “flood” aloud.

fields.Title: Big Red
fields.Location: Whitney Museum of American Art, New York City

fields.Title: One and Three Chairs
fields.Location: Museum of Modern Art, New York City
fields.Captions: A chair, a photograph of that chair, and the dictionary definition of “chair”, installed side by side.

fields.Title: Parthenon Frieze
fields.Location: British Museum, London and Acropolis Museum, Athens
fields.Captions: The Panathenaic procession: 160 metres of low relief that ran round the top of the temple wall, most of it now in the British Museum.

fields.Title: Sculptures of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
fields.Captions: Colossal figures, usually called Mausolus and Artemisia, from the tomb that gave us the word mausoleum.

fields.Title: Arch of Constantine
fields.Captions: A triple triumphal arch beside the Colosseum, built largely out of sculpture stripped from earlier monuments.

fields.Title: Wall paintings from Dura-Europos
fields.Location: Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven
fields.Captions: Biblical scenes from a synagogue on the Euphrates, painted with human figures where nobody expected to find any.

fields.Title: Vienna Genesis
fields.Captions: A Greek Genesis written in silver ink on purple-dyed vellum, with a painted strip along the foot of each page.

fields.Title: Faiyum mummy portraits
fields.Captions: Encaustic panel portraits bound into the wrappings of Roman-era Egyptian mummies -- the earliest painted faces that look back at you.

fields.Title: Sutton Hoo helmet
fields.Captions: The iron helmet and face mask from an Anglo-Saxon ship burial, rebuilt from hundreds of fragments.

fields.Title: Ruthwell Cross
fields.Captions: An Anglo-Saxon preaching cross carved with vine scroll and with runes from The Dream of the Rood.

fields.Title: Utrecht Psalter
fields.Captions: Every psalm illustrated in nervous pen line, taken literally image by image; copied and recopied for centuries.

fields.Title: Bernward Doors
fields.Captions: Two bronze doors, each cast in a single piece for Hildesheim, with Genesis on one leaf facing the life of Christ on the other.

fields.Title: Last Judgement tympanum
fields.Captions: Autun's west doorway, signed in Latin by its sculptor beneath Christ's feet; the elongated damned are weighed in a scale.

fields.Title: The Cloisters Cross
fields.Captions: A walrus-ivory altar cross carved with ninety-two figures and about as many inscriptions.

fields.Title: Klosterneuburg Altar
fields.Captions: Fifty-one champlevé enamel plaques pairing Old and New Testament scenes; it began life as a pulpit front.

fields.Title: Six Persimmons
fields.Captions: Six fruit in ink on paper, each differently spaced and inked; a Chan painting kept in a Kyoto temple.

fields.Title: Apocalypse Tapestry
fields.Captions: Six enormous woven hangings of Revelation, over a hundred metres of them, made for the Duke of Anjou.

fields.Title: Pietà of Villeneuve-lès-Avignon
fields.Captions: A gold-ground Pietà with the donor kneeling at the left; the sharpest French panel painting of its century.

fields.Title: St Mary Altarpiece
fields.Captions: A limewood polyptych over thirteen metres high in Kraków, its central shrine showing the Dormition of the Virgin.

fields.Title: Tomb of Henry VII and Elizabeth of York
Fontaine des Innocents reliefs
fields.Captions: Elongated water nymphs in shallow relief, carved for a Paris fountain in the French Mannerist manner.

fields.Title: The Sacrifice of Isaac
fields.Series: [competition panel for the Florence Baptistery's north doors]
fields.Notes: The winning entry in the 1401 competition for the Florence Baptistery doors, cast largely in a single piece and with less bronze than Filippo Brunelleschi's. Its sculptor spent the next 21 years on the north doors, then 27 on the east doors, which Michelangelo called the Gates of Paradise.
fields.TitleShared: Museo Nazionale del Bargello, Florence · 1401–1402 · the winning entry

fields.Title: The Flight into Egypt
fields.Notes: Painted in Rome on a small copper plate; the night sky shows the Milky Way and the Moon's surface in unusual detail, with identifiable constellations.

fields.Title: Fortitude
fields.Location: Oratorio del Rosario di San Domenico, Palermo
fields.Notes: One of the allegorical Virtues modelled in white stucco for the Rosary oratories of Palermo.

fields.Title: Jacques-Louis David
fields.Notes: His pupils included Ingres, Gros, and Girodet.
fields.Description: French Neoclassical painter who voted for the king's execution, staged the festivals of the Revolution, painted its murdered martyr slumped in a bathtub, and ended as Napoleon's first painter before dying in exile in Brussels.
fields.Captions: Jacques-Louis David
fields.Works: The Death of Marat; Oath of the Horatii; The Death of Socrates; Napoleon Crossing the Alps; The Coronation of Napoleon

fields.Title: Michelangelo
fields.Notes: Giorgio Vasari called him “il Divino”; he also wrote over 300 sonnets and madrigals.
fields.Description: Florentine sculptor, painter, and architect who carved a colossal marble shepherd-king from a block others had abandoned, painted a chapel ceiling from scaffolding for four years, and designed the dome of St. Peter's.
fields.Captions: Michelangelo
fields.Works: David; Sistine Chapel ceiling; The Last Judgment; Pietà; Moses

fields.Title: Salvador Dalí
fields.Notes: His wife and muse Gala had earlier been married to the poet Paul Éluard.
fields.Description: Catalan Surrealist with an upturned waxed moustache who devised the “paranoiac-critical method”, co-made the film Un Chien Andalou with Luis Buñuel, and painted soft watches draped over a Cadaqués landscape.
fields.Captions: Salvador Dalí
fields.Works: The Persistence of Memory; Swans Reflecting Elephants; Christ of Saint John of the Cross; Soft Construction with Boiled Beans; Lobster Telephone

fields.Title: Raphael
fields.Notes: He was buried in the Pantheon in Rome.
fields.Description: High Renaissance painter from Urbino who decorated the papal Stanze for Julius II, gathered the philosophers of Greece under a vaulted hall in one fresco, and died on his 37th birthday.
fields.Captions: Raphael
fields.Works: The School of Athens; Sistine Madonna; The Transfiguration; Portrait of Baldassare Castiglione; La Fornarina

fields.Title: Caravaggio
fields.Notes: His followers across Europe are called Caravaggisti.
fields.Description: Lombard painter of violent chiaroscuro who used street people as models for saints, killed Ranuccio Tomassoni in a brawl, fled Rome for Naples, Malta, and Sicily, and died on the way back to seek a pardon.
fields.Captions: Caravaggio
fields.Works: The Calling of Saint Matthew; Judith Beheading Holofernes; The Supper at Emmaus; The Entombment of Christ; David with the Head of Goliath; Bacchus

fields.Title: René Magritte
fields.Notes: His mother drowned herself in the Sambre when he was thirteen.
fields.Description: Belgian Surrealist who wrote “this is not a pipe” beneath a pipe, painted bowler-hatted men raining from the sky and a face hidden by an apple, and worked for years as a wallpaper and advertising designer.
fields.Captions: René Magritte
fields.Works: The Treachery of Images; The Son of Man; Golconda; The Lovers; Empire of Light; Time Transfixed

fields.Title: Johannes Vermeer
fields.Notes: Han van Meegeren sold forgeries of his work to Hermann Göring.
fields.Description: Delft painter of quiet interiors lit from a window at the left, who used costly ultramarine and possibly a camera obscura, left only about 35 paintings, and died in debt; Théophile Thoré-Bürger rediscovered him in the 1860s.
fields.Captions: Possible self-portrait, from The Procuress
fields.Works: Girl with a Pearl Earring; The Milkmaid; View of Delft; The Art of Painting; The Astronomer; Woman Holding a Balance

fields.Title: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
fields.Notes: His rival was the architect Francesco Borromini.
fields.Description: Baroque sculptor and architect who made marble look like flesh as a pursued nymph turns into a laurel, built the colonnade of St. Peter's Square and the bronze canopy over its altar, and designed a fountain of four rivers in the Piazza Navona.
fields.Captions: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
fields.Works: Ecstasy of Saint Teresa; Apollo and Daphne; The Rape of Proserpina; St. Peter's Baldachin; Fountain of the Four Rivers; David

fields.Title: Edward Hopper
fields.Notes: He studied under Robert Henri.
fields.Description: American realist of urban loneliness who painted a late-night diner seen through a curved window, empty Sunday storefronts, and an usherette in a movie theatre, nearly always using his wife Josephine as the model for every woman.
fields.Captions: Edward Hopper
fields.Works: Nighthawks; Early Sunday Morning; Automat; Gas; New York Movie; Chop Suey

fields.Title: Donatello
fields.Notes: He pioneered the shallow relief called rilievo schiacciato.
fields.Description: Florentine sculptor who made the first free-standing bronze nude since antiquity, a boyish hero in a shepherd's hat standing on a giant's head, plus a gaunt, wooden penitent Magdalene and an equestrian general in Padua.
fields.Captions: Donatello
fields.Works: David (bronze); Gattamelata; Penitent Magdalene; St. George; Judith and Holofernes; Feast of Herod

fields.Title: Constantin Brâncuşi
fields.Notes: Brancusi v. United States (1928) ruled the bird was art.
fields.Description: Romanian sculptor who walked much of the way to Paris, left Rodin's studio saying nothing grows in the shadow of great trees, and reduced a bird to a polished bronze blade that U.S. customs tried to tax as metal.
fields.Captions: Constantin Brâncuşi
fields.Works: Bird in Space; The Kiss; Endless Column; Sleeping Muse; Mademoiselle Pogany; Princess X

fields.Title: Eugène Delacroix
fields.Notes: He was rumoured to be Talleyrand's son; Ingres was his great rival.
fields.Description: French Romantic painter who put a bare-breasted allegory with a tricolour over the barricades of 1830, painted an Assyrian king ordering his harem slaughtered, travelled to Morocco, and kept a celebrated journal.
fields.Captions: Eugène Delacroix
fields.Works: Liberty Leading the People; The Death of Sardanapalus; The Massacre at Chios; Women of Algiers in their Apartment; The Barque of Dante

fields.Title: Vincent van Gogh
fields.Notes: He sold almost nothing in his lifetime and shot himself at Auvers-sur-Oise.
fields.Description: Dutch painter supported by his brother Theo, who worked in the Borinage as a lay preacher, shared the Yellow House in Arles with Gauguin until he cut off part of his own ear, and painted a swirling night sky from the asylum at Saint-Rémy.
fields.Captions: Vincent van Gogh
fields.Works: The Starry Night; Sunflowers; The Potato Eaters; Café Terrace at Night; Wheatfield with Crows; The Night Café; Bedroom in Arles

fields.Title: Pablo Picasso
fields.Notes: Dora Maar, Marie-Thérèse Walter, and Françoise Gilot were among his partners.
fields.Description: Málaga-born painter who passed through Blue and Rose periods, co-founded Cubism with Georges Braque, painted five Barcelona prostitutes with mask-like faces, and answered the bombing of a Basque town with a vast grey mural.
fields.Captions: Pablo Picasso
fields.Works: Guernica; Les Demoiselles d'Avignon; The Old Guitarist; Portrait of Gertrude Stein; Three Musicians; Bull's Head

fields.Title: Franz Marc
fields.Notes: The Tower of Blue Horses disappeared after the Nazis seized it as “degenerate”.
fields.Description: German Expressionist who co-founded Der Blaue Reiter with Kandinsky, gave colours meanings (blue masculine and spiritual, yellow feminine), painted animals, above all horses, in pure colour, and was killed at Verdun.
fields.Captions: Franz Marc
fields.Works: The Large Blue Horses; Blue Horse I; The Yellow Cow; Fate of the Animals; The Tower of Blue Horses; Fighting Forms

fields.Title: Albrecht Dürer
fields.Notes: His two trips to Italy carried the Renaissance north.
fields.Description: Nuremberg painter and printmaker who drew a rhinoceros he never saw, portrayed himself frontally like Christ, engraved a knight riding past Death and the Devil, and signed everything with an A enclosing a D.
fields.Captions: Albrecht Dürer
fields.Works: Melencolia I; Self-Portrait (1500); Rhinoceros; Knight, Death and the Devil; Young Hare; The Four Horsemen; Adam and Eve

fields.Title: Rembrandt
fields.Notes: Hendrickje Stoffels, his later companion, was censured by the church for living with him.
fields.Description: Leiden-born Amsterdam painter who painted dozens of self-portraits, a dissection lesson, and a civic militia company marching out of shadow, and went bankrupt in the years after his wife Saskia died.
fields.Captions: Rembrandt
fields.Works: The Night Watch; The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp; The Return of the Prodigal Son; Self-Portrait with Two Circles; Syndics of the Drapers' Guild; Bathsheba at Her Bath

fields.Title: Marc Chagall
fields.Notes: His wife Bella Rosenfeld floats beside him in The Birthday.
fields.Description: Painter from Vitebsk whose dreamlike canvases float fiddlers, goats, and lovers over Jewish villages; he ran an art school where Malevich ousted him, and later made stained glass for Jerusalem and the Paris Opéra ceiling.
fields.Captions: Marc Chagall
fields.Works: I and the Village; The Birthday; The Fiddler; White Crucifixion; Over the Town; Paris Opéra ceiling

fields.Title: Frida Kahlo
fields.Notes: Her Casa Azul in Coyoacán is now her museum; Trotsky lived there in 1937.
fields.Description: Mexican painter crippled by polio and a bus accident, who painted herself in a steel corset with a shattered column for a spine, twice married Diego Rivera, and wore Tehuana dress.
fields.Captions: Frida Kahlo
fields.Works: The Two Fridas; The Broken Column; Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird; Henry Ford Hospital; Frieda and Diego Rivera

fields.Title: Edvard Munch
fields.Notes: Two versions of his most famous work were stolen in 1994 and 2004; both were recovered.
fields.Description: Norwegian Symbolist haunted by the deaths of his mother and sister, who painted a skeletal figure clutching its face under a blood-red sky on an Oslo fjord, and arranged his canvases into a Frieze of Life.
fields.Captions: Edvard Munch
fields.Works: The Scream; Madonna; The Sick Child; Vampire; The Dance of Life; Puberty

fields.Title: James McNeill Whistler
fields.Notes: He was expelled from West Point for failing chemistry.
fields.Description: Massachusetts-born painter in London who gave his paintings musical titles, sued John Ruskin for libel over “flinging a pot of paint in the public's face” and won a farthing, and decorated the Peacock Room.
fields.Captions: James McNeill Whistler
fields.Works: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1; Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket; Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl; The Peacock Room

fields.Title: Grant Wood
fields.Notes: He, Thomas Hart Benton, and John Steuart Curry were the Regionalist triumvirate.
fields.Description: Iowa Regionalist who posed his sister and his dentist in front of a farmhouse window, painted Paul Revere's ride from above and Parson Weems pulling back a curtain on a cherry tree.
fields.Captions: Grant Wood
fields.Works: American Gothic; The Midnight Ride of Paul Revere; Parson Weems' Fable; Daughters of Revolution; Stone City, Iowa

fields.Title: Titian
fields.Notes: Charles V is said to have stooped to pick up the brush he dropped.
fields.Description: Venetian painter who finished Giorgione's sleeping Venus, painted Charles V at Mühlberg, sent Philip II a set of mythological “poesie”, and in old age painted with his fingers.
fields.Captions: Titian
fields.Works: Venus of Urbino; Assumption of the Virgin; Bacchus and Ariadne; Sacred and Profane Love; Equestrian Portrait of Charles V; The Flaying of Marsyas

fields.Title: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
fields.Notes: His sons Pieter the Younger and Jan the Elder founded a dynasty of painters.
fields.Description: Flemish painter nicknamed “Peasant”, who painted a series of the months with hunters returning over snow, a tiny drowning Icarus beside a ploughman, and a Tower of Babel modelled on the Colosseum.
fields.Captions: Possible self-portrait, The Painter and the Buyer
fields.Works: The Hunters in the Snow; Landscape with the Fall of Icarus; The Tower of Babel; Netherlandish Proverbs; The Peasant Wedding; The Triumph of Death

fields.Title: Lucas Cranach the Elder
fields.Notes: He also ran a pharmacy and a printing press and served as mayor of Wittenberg.
fields.Description: Court painter to the Electors of Saxony at Wittenberg who painted repeated portraits of his friend Martin Luther, slender Venuses and Eves, and signed with a winged serpent.
fields.Captions: Lucas Cranach the Elder
fields.Works: Portrait of Martin Luther; Adam and Eve; The Judgment of Paris; The Fountain of Youth; Venus and Cupid

fields.Title: Marcel Duchamp
fields.Notes: His female alter ego was Rrose Sélavy.
fields.Description: French artist who signed a urinal “R. Mutt”, painted a nude as a cascade of mechanical planes, drew a moustache on the Mona Lisa, and supposedly gave up art for chess.
fields.Captions: Marcel Duchamp
fields.Works: Fountain; Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2; The Large Glass; L.H.O.O.Q.; Bicycle Wheel; Étant donnés

fields.Title: Auguste Rodin
fields.Notes: The École des Beaux-Arts rejected him three times.
fields.Description: French sculptor accused of casting his first life-size bronze from a live model, who spent decades on a portal for a decorative-arts museum based on Dante and had a stormy affair with his pupil Camille Claudel.
fields.Captions: Auguste Rodin
fields.Works: The Thinker; The Gates of Hell; The Kiss; The Burghers of Calais; Monument to Balzac; The Age of Bronze

fields.Title: Leonardo da Vinci
fields.Notes: Vasari says he painted an angel in Verrocchio's Baptism of Christ.
fields.Description: Tuscan polymath who trained under Verrocchio, filled notebooks in mirror writing, perfected sfumato, painted a deteriorating mural of Christ's last meal in a Milan refectory, and died at Amboise in the service of Francis I.
fields.Captions: Leonardo da Vinci
fields.Works: Mona Lisa; The Last Supper; Vitruvian Man; Lady with an Ermine; The Virgin of the Rocks; Salvator Mundi

fields.Title: Peter Paul Rubens
fields.Notes: He painted the Banqueting House ceiling in Whitehall.
fields.Description: Antwerp Baroque painter and diplomat, knighted by both Charles I and Philip IV, who ran a vast workshop, painted a 24-canvas cycle on Marie de' Medici's life, and gave his name to fleshy female nudes.
fields.Captions: Peter Paul Rubens
fields.Works: The Elevation of the Cross; The Descent from the Cross; The Marie de' Medici Cycle; The Judgment of Paris; The Three Graces; Massacre of the Innocents

fields.Title: Andy Warhol
fields.Notes: He predicted that everyone would be world-famous for 15 minutes.
fields.Description: Pittsburgh-born Pop artist who ran the Factory, silkscreened soup cans, Marilyn Monroe, and car crashes, managed the Velvet Underground, and was shot by Valerie Solanas in 1968.
fields.Captions: Andy Warhol
fields.Works: Campbell's Soup Cans; Marilyn Diptych; Shot Marilyns; Brillo Box; Death and Disaster series; Empire

fields.Title: Winslow Homer
fields.Notes: A stay at Cullercoats in England turned him to the sea.
fields.Description: American painter who drew the Civil War for Harper's Weekly, then painted the sea from Prouts Neck, Maine, including a sailor adrift among sharks and a rescuer carrying a fainting woman along a breeches-buoy line.
fields.Captions: Winslow Homer
fields.Works: The Gulf Stream; Snap the Whip; Breezing Up (A Fair Wind); Prisoners from the Front; The Fox Hunt; The Life Line

fields.Title: Sandro Botticelli
fields.Notes: He painted frescoes on the Sistine Chapel walls and illustrated Dante.
fields.Description: Florentine painter for the Medici who painted a goddess arriving on a scallop shell and an orange grove of mythology, then, it is said, burned his own work in Savonarola's bonfire of the vanities.
fields.Captions: Sandro Botticelli
fields.Works: The Birth of Venus; Primavera; Venus and Mars; Adoration of the Magi; Pallas and the Centaur; Mystic Nativity

fields.Title: Paul Cézanne
fields.Notes: Zola's novel L'Œuvre ended their friendship.
fields.Description: Aix-en-Provence painter, a childhood friend of Émile Zola, who painted the same limestone mountain over 60 times, apples on tilted tables, and card-playing peasants, and said nature should be treated as cylinder, sphere, and cone.
fields.Captions: Paul Cézanne in 1906, photographed by Gertrud Osthaus
fields.Works: Mont Sainte-Victoire; The Card Players; The Large Bathers; Still Life with Apples; The Basket of Apples

fields.Title: Édouard Manet
fields.Notes: Berthe Morisot married his brother Eugène.
fields.Description: Parisian painter whose picnic of clothed men and a nude woman scandalized the Salon des Refusés, who painted Victorine Meurent as a courtesan with a black ribbon at her throat, and a barmaid before a mirror at the Folies-Bergère.
fields.Captions: Édouard Manet
fields.Works: Olympia; Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe; A Bar at the Folies-Bergère; The Execution of Emperor Maximilian; Music in the Tuileries

fields.Title: John Singer Sargent
fields.Notes: He painted murals for the Boston Public Library.
fields.Description: Florence-born American portraitist whose picture of Virginie Gautreau with a slipped strap drove him from Paris to London; he also painted two girls lighting lanterns among lilies and the gassed soldiers of World War I.
fields.Captions: John Singer Sargent
fields.Works: Madame X; Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose; The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit; Gassed; El Jaleo

fields.Title: Henri Matisse
fields.Notes: He designed the Chapelle du Rosaire at Vence.
fields.Description: Leader of the Fauves, who painted his wife with a green stripe down her face, a ring of nude dancers for Sergei Shchukin, and, when surgery left him in a wheelchair, cut shapes from painted paper.
fields.Captions: Henri Matisse
fields.Works: The Dance; Woman with a Hat; The Joy of Life; The Red Studio; Blue Nudes; The Snail; Jazz

fields.Title: Francisco Goya
fields.Notes: He died in exile in Bordeaux.
fields.Description: Spanish court painter to Charles IV who went deaf, etched the horrors of the Peninsular War, painted a Madrid firing squad of 3 May 1808, and covered the walls of his house with the Black Paintings.
fields.Captions: Francisco Goya
fields.Works: The Third of May 1808; Saturn Devouring His Son; The Nude Maja; The Family of Charles IV; The Disasters of War; The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters

fields.Title: El Greco
fields.Notes: His name was Domenikos Theotokopoulos.
fields.Description: Cretan-born painter trained as an icon painter and in Venice, who settled in Toledo, stretched his figures into flickering elongated forms, and painted a count's funeral attended by saints.
fields.Captions: El Greco
fields.Works: The Burial of the Count of Orgaz; View of Toledo; The Disrobing of Christ; The Opening of the Fifth Seal; Portrait of a Cardinal

fields.Title: J.M.W. Turner
fields.Notes: John Ruskin championed him; a Tate prize bears his name.
fields.Description: London painter of light and weather who supposedly had himself lashed to a mast in a snowstorm, painted a warship towed to her breaking-up and a train in the rain, and left his work to the nation.
fields.Captions: J.M.W. Turner
fields.Works: The Fighting Temeraire; Rain, Steam and Speed; The Slave Ship; Snow Storm: Hannibal and his Army Crossing the Alps; The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons

fields.Title: Gustave Courbet
fields.Notes: He died in Switzerland, still owing the cost of rebuilding the column.
fields.Description: French Realist from Ornans who mounted his own Pavilion of Realism, painted a huge village funeral and two stone-breakers, and was jailed and exiled after the Paris Commune toppled the Vendôme Column.
fields.Captions: Gustave Courbet
fields.Works: A Burial at Ornans; The Stone Breakers; The Painter's Studio; Bonjour, Monsieur Courbet; The Origin of the World; The Desperate Man

fields.Title: Georgia O'Keeffe
fields.Notes: Stieglitz photographed her more than 300 times.
fields.Description: American modernist who married the photographer Alfred Stieglitz, painted enormous close-up flowers and bleached cow skulls, and settled at Ghost Ranch and Abiquiú in New Mexico.
fields.Captions: Georgia O'Keeffe
fields.Works: Jimson Weed/White Flower No. 1; Black Iris; Cow's Skull: Red, White, and Blue; Radiator Building, Night, New York; Sky Above Clouds IV

fields.Title: Edgar Degas
fields.Notes: Failing eyesight turned him to pastel and sculpture.
fields.Description: Parisian painter who disliked the name Impressionist, drew ballet dancers in rehearsal and women bathing, painted a pair of absinthe drinkers, and modelled a wax dancer dressed in a real tutu.
fields.Captions: Edgar Degas
fields.Works: The Dance Class; Little Dancer of Fourteen Years; L'Absinthe; The Bellelli Family; A Cotton Office in New Orleans; The Tub

fields.Title: Alexander Calder
fields.Notes: Jean Arp called his static works stabiles.
fields.Description: American sculptor who trained as an engineer, performed a wire circus in Paris, and invented hanging sculptures moved by air, which Duchamp named mobiles.
fields.Captions: Alexander Calder with Maria Lluïsa Borràs
fields.Works: Lobster Trap and Fish Tail; Calder's Circus; Flamingo; Mercury Fountain; Arc of Petals

fields.Title: Thomas Cole
fields.Notes: His pupil Frederic Edwin Church continued the school.
fields.Description: English-born American founder of the Hudson River School, who painted an oxbow of the Connecticut River under a passing storm and a five-canvas cycle on the rise and fall of an empire.
fields.Captions: Thomas Cole
fields.Works: The Oxbow; The Course of Empire; The Voyage of Life; Kaaterskill Falls

fields.Title: Jackson Pollock
fields.Notes: Harold Rosenberg coined “action painting” with him in mind; he was married to Lee Krasner.
fields.Description: Wyoming-born Abstract Expressionist who laid canvas on the floor of a barn in Springs, Long Island, and poured and dripped paint onto it, was photographed at work by Hans Namuth, and died in a drunk-driving crash.
fields.Captions: Jackson Pollock, photographed by Hans Namuth
fields.Works: Autumn Rhythm (Number 30); Blue Poles; Lavender Mist; One: Number 31, 1950; Mural; Convergence

fields.Title: Andrew Wyeth
fields.Notes: His father was the illustrator N. C. Wyeth.
fields.Description: American realist of Chadds Ford and Cushing, Maine, who painted his disabled neighbour crawling up a field toward a farmhouse and secretly made over 200 studies of a German neighbour named Helga.
fields.Captions: Andrew Wyeth, wearing the National Medal of Arts, with his wife, Betsy (left), and Laura Bush, 2007
fields.Works: Christina's World; The Helga Pictures; Wind from the Sea; Winter 1946

fields.Title: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
fields.Notes: His son Jean became a film director.
fields.Description: Impressionist who began as a porcelain painter, painted dappled Sunday dancers at a Montmartre open-air café and friends lunching on a boating balcony, and kept painting with arthritis-crippled hands.
fields.Captions: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
fields.Works: Bal du moulin de la Galette; Luncheon of the Boating Party; The Umbrellas; The Large Bathers; La Loge

fields.Title: Paul Gauguin
fields.Notes: He wrote the memoir Noa Noa.
fields.Description: French stockbroker turned painter who led the Pont-Aven group in Brittany, quarrelled with van Gogh in Arles, and moved to Tahiti and the Marquesas, where he painted a vast canvas asking where we come from.
fields.Captions: Paul Gauguin
fields.Works: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?; Vision after the Sermon; The Yellow Christ; Spirit of the Dead Watching; Nevermore

fields.Title: Diego Velázquez
fields.Notes: He was made a knight of the Order of Santiago; the red cross on his chest in Las Meninas was added later.
fields.Description: Seville-born court painter to Philip IV who painted the Infanta Margarita with her maids and himself at the easel, a pope who called the portrait “too true”, and the Spanish receiving the keys of a Dutch city.
fields.Captions: Diego Velázquez
fields.Works: Las Meninas; Portrait of Innocent X; The Surrender of Breda; Rokeby Venus; Las Hilanderas; An Old Woman Cooking Eggs

fields.Title: Mary Cassatt
fields.Notes: Her colour prints imitated Japanese woodblocks.
fields.Description: Pittsburgh-born painter in Paris, the only American to exhibit with the Impressionists, invited by Degas, who painted mothers bathing children and a girl sprawled in a blue armchair.
fields.Captions: Mary Cassatt
fields.Works: The Child's Bath; Little Girl in a Blue Armchair; In the Loge; The Boating Party; Mother and Child

fields.Title: Jan van Eyck
fields.Notes: His motto was “Als ich can” (“As I can”).
fields.Description: Bruges painter to Philip the Good who perfected oil glazes, finished the Ghent Altarpiece begun by his brother Hubert, and signed a convex mirror in a double portrait with the words “was here, 1434”.
fields.Captions: Possible self-portrait, Portrait of a Man in a Red Turban
fields.Works: The Arnolfini Portrait; Ghent Altarpiece; Madonna of Chancellor Rolin; Portrait of a Man in a Red Turban; Madonna of Canon van der Paele

fields.Title: Hieronymus Bosch
fields.Notes: Philip II of Spain collected him, which is why so much of his work is in the Prado.
fields.Description: Painter from a Brabant cathedral town, which gave him his name, whose triptychs teem with hybrid monsters and tortured sinners, including a paradise of giant fruit and naked lovers and a hell of musical instruments.
fields.Captions: Hieronymus Bosch
fields.Works: The Garden of Earthly Delights; The Haywain Triptych; The Temptation of St. Anthony; The Seven Deadly Sins; Ship of Fools

fields.Title: Diego Rivera
fields.Notes: He, José Clemente Orozco, and David Alfaro Siqueiros were “los tres grandes”.
fields.Description: Mexican muralist, twice married to Frida Kahlo, who painted Detroit's car industry at the Institute of Arts and had his Rockefeller Center mural destroyed because it included Lenin.
fields.Captions: Diego Rivera
fields.Works: Detroit Industry Murals; Man at the Crossroads; History of Mexico (National Palace); The Flower Carrier; Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in the Alameda Park

fields.Title: Caspar David Friedrich
fields.Notes: His brother drowned saving him when they fell through ice as boys.
fields.Description: Pomeranian Romantic who painted figures from behind as they gaze at nature (the Rückenfigur), a wanderer above clouds, a ship crushed by Arctic ice, and a monk before a vast grey sea.
fields.Captions: Caspar David Friedrich
fields.Works: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog; The Sea of Ice; The Monk by the Sea; Chalk Cliffs on Rügen; Abbey in the Oakwood; The Cross in the Mountains

fields.Title: Thomas Eakins
fields.Notes: He worked with Muybridge on motion photography.
fields.Description: Philadelphia realist who painted a surgeon lecturing in a bloody operating theatre, rowers on the Schuylkill, and naked boys at a swimming hole; he was forced out of the Pennsylvania Academy for removing a male model's loincloth before female students.
fields.Captions: Thomas Eakins
fields.Works: The Gross Clinic; The Agnew Clinic; Max Schmitt in a Single Scull; The Swimming Hole; William Rush Carving His Allegorical Figure

fields.Title: Joan Miró
fields.Notes: Hemingway bought The Farm.
fields.Description: Catalan painter of biomorphic shapes, stars, and eyes on flat colour, who painted a Catalan farm in obsessive detail, a harlequin's carnival, and a series of 23 Constellations during World War II.
fields.Captions: Joan Miró
fields.Works: The Farm; Harlequin's Carnival; Constellations; Dog Barking at the Moon; The Reaper; Blue I–III

fields.Title: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres
fields.Description: Pupil of David and champion of line over colour, rival of Delacroix, who gave a reclining harem woman three extra vertebrae and played the violin, so that his name means a hobby in French.
fields.Captions: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres
fields.Works: Grande Odalisque; The Turkish Bath; The Valpinçon Bather; Napoleon I on his Imperial Throne; Portrait of Monsieur Bertin; The Apotheosis of Homer

fields.Title: Hans Holbein the Younger
fields.Notes: Henry disliked Anne of Cleves in person after seeing her portrait.
fields.Description: Augsburg-born painter who worked in Basel and London, portrayed Erasmus and Thomas More, became Henry VIII's court painter, and hid a distorted skull at the feet of two French envoys.
fields.Captions: Hans Holbein the Younger
fields.Works: The Ambassadors; Portrait of Henry VIII; The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb; Portrait of Erasmus; Portrait of Anne of Cleves; Dance of Death woodcuts

fields.Title: Claude Monet
fields.Notes: The Orangerie in Paris holds his great water-lily panels.
fields.Description: Impressionist whose view of Le Havre harbour gave the movement its name, who painted series of haystacks, poplars, and Rouen Cathedral at different hours, and built a Japanese bridge over a lily pond at Giverny.
fields.Captions: Claude Monet
fields.Works: Impression, Sunrise; Water Lilies; Haystacks; Rouen Cathedral series; Woman with a Parasol; La Gare Saint-Lazare

fields.Title: John Constable
fields.Notes: Delacroix is said to have repainted his Massacre at Chios after seeing his work.
fields.Description: Suffolk landscape painter of the Stour valley who made “six-footers”, cloud studies at Hampstead, and a hay wagon crossing a mill stream, and was better received at the 1824 Paris Salon than at home.
fields.Captions: John Constable
fields.Works: The Hay Wain; Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds; The White Horse; Flatford Mill; Wivenhoe Park

fields.Title: William Hogarth
fields.Notes: His treatise The Analysis of Beauty praised the “line of beauty”.
fields.Description: London satirist whose engraved “modern moral subjects” follow a harlot, a rake, and an arranged marriage to ruin; he campaigned for a Copyright Act and contrasted two streets, one of beer and one of gin.
fields.Captions: William Hogarth
fields.Works: A Rake's Progress; A Harlot's Progress; Marriage A-la-Mode; Gin Lane; Beer Street; The Shrimp Girl

fields.Title: Artemisia Gentileschi
fields.Notes: She worked for Charles I in London alongside her father.
fields.Description: Roman Caravaggist, daughter of Orazio, who testified under thumbscrew torture against the painter Agostino Tassi and became the first woman in Florence's Accademia delle Arti del Disegno.
fields.Captions: Artemisia Gentileschi
fields.Works: Judith Slaying Holofernes; Susanna and the Elders; Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting; Judith and her Maidservant

fields.Title: Andrea Mantegna
fields.Notes: His Triumphs of Caesar hang at Hampton Court.
fields.Description: Paduan painter, brother-in-law of Giovanni Bellini, who painted a dead Christ in extreme foreshortening from the feet and a ceiling oculus of courtiers peering down in the Gonzagas' palace at Mantua.
fields.Captions: Andrea Mantegna
fields.Works: Lamentation over the Dead Christ; Camera degli Sposi; St. Sebastian; The Triumphs of Caesar; Parnassus

fields.Title: Nicolas Poussin
fields.Notes: Anthony Blunt was his great scholar.
fields.Description: French Classical painter who spent most of his life in Rome, painted shepherds reading a tomb inscription in Arcadia, and set out a theory of “modes” for painting; his followers fought the Rubénistes.
fields.Captions: Nicolas Poussin
fields.Works: Et in Arcadia ego; The Abduction of the Sabine Women; A Dance to the Music of Time; Landscape with the Ashes of Phocion; The Holy Family on the Steps

fields.Title: Katsushika Hokusai
fields.Notes: He called himself “the old man mad about painting”.
fields.Description: Edo ukiyo-e artist who used some 30 names, published sketchbooks of manga, drew an octopus with a pearl diver, and made a woodblock series of views of Japan's highest mountain, one behind a towering wave.
fields.Captions: Katsushika Hokusai
fields.Works: The Great Wave off Kanagawa; Fine Wind, Clear Morning; Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji; The Dream of the Fisherman's Wife; Hokusai Manga

fields.Title: Mark Rothko
fields.Notes: He killed himself in his studio in 1970, and his estate became a notorious lawsuit.
fields.Description: Latvian-born American Colour Field painter of stacked, soft-edged rectangles, who withdrew murals commissioned for the Four Seasons restaurant and made dark canvases for a non-denominational chapel in Houston.
fields.Captions: Mark Rothko
fields.Works: Seagram Murals; Rothko Chapel; No. 61 (Rust and Blue); Orange, Red, Yellow; Slow Swirl at the Edge of the Sea

fields.Title: Gustav Klimt
fields.Notes: Maria Altmann recovered the Bloch-Bauer portrait from Austria in 2006.
fields.Description: First president of the Vienna Secession, who painted in gold leaf, including a kissing couple in patterned robes and Adele Bloch-Bauer, and whose university ceiling paintings were attacked as pornographic.
fields.Captions: Gustav Klimt with one of his cats
fields.Works: The Kiss; Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I; The Beethoven Frieze; Judith and the Head of Holofernes; Danaë; Death and Life

fields.Title: Piet Mondrian
fields.Notes: He called his theory Neoplasticism.
fields.Description: Dutch painter who reduced trees to grids, co-founded De Stijl with Theo van Doesburg and broke with him over diagonals, and ended in New York painting yellow grids after boogie-woogie.
fields.Captions: Piet Mondrian, Self-Portrait, 1918
fields.Works: Composition with Red, Blue, and Yellow; Broadway Boogie Woogie; Victory Boogie Woogie; The Grey Tree; New York City I

fields.Title: Olmec colossal heads
fields.Notes: Seventeen are known, from four sites, most of them San Lorenzo and La Venta. Each wears a close-fitting helmet and is thought to portray a particular ruler; the basalt was hauled from the Tuxtla Mountains.
fields.Captions: A head from La Venta

fields.Title: Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains
fields.Location: National Palace Museum, Taipei; Zhejiang Provincial Museum, Hangzhou
fields.Style: Yuan Literati Painting; Ink on paper
fields.Notes: A collector tried to burn it on his deathbed in 1650; it survived in two pieces, now on opposite sides of the Taiwan Strait, and was shown reunited in Taipei in 2011.
fields.Captions: A section of the longer part, the Master Wuyong scroll

fields.Title: Lamassu
fields.Notes: Human-headed winged bulls or lions that guarded Assyrian palace gateways. Most have five legs, so that they look complete from the front and from the side.
fields.Captions: The pair from Ashurnasirpal II's palace at Nimrud, British Museum | One of Sargon II's pair from Khorsabad, Louvre

fields.Title: The Court of Gayumars
fields.Style: Safavid Persian Painting; Opaque watercolour, ink, and gold on paper
fields.Notes: The most celebrated page of the most lavish Book of Kings ever made, begun for Shah Ismail I and given away by his son to the Ottoman sultan; the manuscript was broken up in the 20th century.
fields.Captions: The first king of the Shahnameh holding court in the mountains

fields.Title: Mughal painting
fields.Notes: Akbar's Hamzanama ran to some 1,400 large pages; Jahangir favoured single-page portraits and natural history, such as Mansur's zebra and turkey.
fields.Description: Miniature painting for the Muslim emperors of India, founded when Humayun brought two Persian masters from the Safavid court and developed under Akbar and Jahangir into a naturalistic, portrait-rich court style.
fields.Captions: A page from Akbar's Hamzanama, c. 1570 | Bichitr, Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings, c. 1615–1618

fields.Title: Narmer Palette
fields.Notes: Found at Hierakonpolis in 1898. The king wears the white crown of Upper Egypt on one face and the red crown of Lower Egypt on the other, so it is read as a record of unification.
fields.Captions: The king smiting a kneeling enemy | Two serpopards with intertwined necks
fields.Clue: A ceremonial siltstone slab for grinding cosmetics shows a king in the white crown smiting an enemy on one face and two long-necked beasts entwined around the grinding hollow on the other.

fields.Title: Gran Cavallo (or Sforza Horse)
fields.Style: High Renaissance; Clay model for an unrealized bronze
fields.Notes: Commissioned in honour of Ludovico's father, Francesco Sforza; the 70 tonnes of bronze set aside for it were cast into cannon in 1494, and French archers used the clay model for target practice in 1499. Nina Akamu's 7.3-metre bronze, after Leonardo's drawings, was unveiled in Milan in 1999.
fields.Captions: Leonardo da Vinci, Study for an Equestrian Monument, c. 1485–1490, Royal Collection | Leonardo da Vinci, the casting mould for the horse's head, Codex Madrid II, c. 1493 | Nina Akamu, Leonardo's Horse, 1999, San Siro racecourse, Milan
fields.Clue: A planned bronze equestrian monument over seven metres tall for Ludovico Sforza, the largest ever attempted, of which only a full-size clay model was made before the metal went into cannon.
